children: reported third-quarter net revenues of RMB309.6 billion, up 3.5%, and its ADRs fell 7.66% to $25.43 at the 4:00 p.m. ET close on November 17. The Chinese e-commerce and logistics group returned to growth, but the core retail engine barely moved.

JD Retail revenue rose 2.9% to RMB258.0 billion with a 5.8% operating margin, slightly below last year. Non-GAAP net income attributable to shareholders climbed to RMB8.3 billion from RMB5.8 billion as New Businesses revenue halved and the segment's losses shrank. On the earnings call, management said electronics and appliances fell 0.7%, food delivery losses narrowed by more than 50%, and higher R&D spending may weigh on near-term margins.

The New Businesses operating loss of RMB9.6 billion still exceeds the RMB8.3 billion of non-GAAP profit, so every yuan of subsidy cut drops almost straight into earnings. That is the bull case, but it relies on spending discipline rather than demand. GuruFocus gives JD.com a GF Score of 74/100, with middling profitability and balance sheet ranks and weak momentum. Its GF Value of $39.88 implies the ADRs trade about 36% below the model, which GuruFocus calls significantly undervalued, though Chinese platforms have often stayed cheap for long stretches. The next test is fourth-quarter results, which will show whether management delivers the promised sharp cut in 2027 food delivery investment.

title: JD.com Stocks Fall 7.66% After Results Show Retail Growth of Just 2.9%
